jobs.title: Technical Oversight - Processing
jobs.descriptionHtml:
About Pylon

America’s $13T mortgage market is one of the most important financial systems in the world. It underwrites the middle class and is the mechanism through which millions of families build wealth. But while every other financial instrument has been simplified to an API call, mortgages are still assembled by hand.

We started from zero and created the first vertically integrated mortgage platform that turns origination into a single API.

Publicly traded companies and the country’s largest originators are already building on Pylon. Revenue is compounding monthly. We’re backed by Peter Thiel, Conversion Capital, QED, Citi, Fifth Wall, and the founders of Ramp, Blend, and Mercury.

Working at Pylon isn’t for those seeking comfort. The people who thrive here have high agency, strong opinions, and a track record of delivering outcomes without direction. Many of us are former founders. We move quickly, challenge each other directly, and take full ownership of results. It’s hard work, but it will be worth it.

Join us in building America’s mortgage rails.

About the Role

We’re seeking a Technical Oversight - Processing with deep mortgage operations experience and strong independent judgment. This is not a traditional customer support or relationship-only role. You will act as a senior operational partner to our originating customers, owning issue resolution end-to-end and ensuring loans move cleanly, compliantly, and predictably through the lifecycle.

You will work directly with customers while collaborating closely with underwriting, processing, product, and engineering to reduce errors, prevent rework, and improve system-driven workflows. This role is ideal for someone who has worked inside the loan file, understands where mortgages break, and is motivated to help build scalable, automated systems that eliminate those failures over time.

We are not a traditional mortgage lender. If you’re excited about operating with rigor today while helping design the future of automated mortgage infrastructure, this role is for you.

Key Responsibilities

Client & Origination Ownership

  • Act as a operational point of contact for originating customers, owning issue resolution from identification through closure

  • Guide customers through the full loan lifecycle, providing clear, accurate direction on requirements, timelines, disclosures and next steps

  • Own the operational health of assigned loans end-to-end, ensuring files progress on schedule and close on time by proactively identifying blockers, driving resolution, and coordinating across internal teams and customers.

  • Proactively manage customer expectations to reduce inbound escalations and uncertainty

Operational Judgment & Risk Prevention

  • Independently evaluate loan scenarios to identify potential structural, disclosure, or compliance risks before they escalate

  • Catch missing, inconsistent, or incorrect inputs that could lead to redisclosures, delays, or downstream rework

  • Provide firm, professional guidance to customers when corrections or process adherence are required

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner closely with underwriting, processing, and closing teams to ensure clean handoffs and aligned execution

  • Serve as a trusted escalation point, reducing leadership involvement by resolving complex or high-stakes issues directly

  • Coordinate with third-party vendors to ensure issues are addressed efficiently, quickly and accurately

Systems & Product Feedback

  • Identify recurring patterns, edge cases, and workflow gaps that impact loan quality or customer experience

  • Collaborate with Product and Engineering to help define requirements, guardrails, and operational acceptance criteria

  • Contribute real-world mortgage insight to improve automation, tooling, and system-driven decisioning

Documentation & Quality

  • Maintain clear, accurate documentation of customer interactions, decisions, and follow-ups

  • Ensure customer-facing communication aligns with regulatory requirements, internal standards, and operational best practices

Qualifications

  • 7+ years of mortgage industry experience, with hands-on roles in processing, underwriting, or a similar operational function

  • Direct experience working loans from application through CTC and closing

  • Hands-on experience with mortgage disclosures, including preparing, reviewing, or validating LEs and CDs, with a strong working knowledge of TRID timing, tolerance categories, and re-disclosure triggers.

  • Ability to independently sanity-check loan structure, including LTV, product eligibility, and basic compliance considerations

  • Prior experience serving as an escalation point for brokers, borrowers, or loan officers

  • Comfortable operating in fast-moving, ambiguous environments where processes are still being built

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to explain complex mortgage concepts clearly and confidently

  • High attention to detail paired with strong problem-solving instincts and sound judgment

What This Role Is Not

  • This is not a call-center or script-based customer support role

  • This is not a traditional CSM focused only on relationship management

  • This is not a sales or loan officer role — there are no commissions or volume-based incentives

  • This role requires independent mortgage judgment, ownership, and accountability

Benefits

Ownership: Meaningful early-stage equity in Pylon
Healthcare: Top-tier medical, vision & dental with support for dependents
401(k): Ability to save for your future
Flexible Time Off: Be on when you’re on and off when you’re off
Hardware Allowance: $2,000 to fix up your workspace
Annual Off-sites: Fully paid for team off-sites in beautiful corners of the world
At-cost Mortgages: We’ll help you finance your next home when you’re ready

About the Role

We are hiring a Technical Oversight - Post Closing to own loan delivery, purchase timelines, and post-closing issue resolution across our investor and whole-loan channels. This role is accountable for ensuring closed loans are delivered cleanly, purchased quickly, and resolved efficiently when issues arise.

You will serve as the primary owner of investor delivery and rebuttals, as well as the main point of contact for sellers whose loans we purchase and the investors we sell to. This is a hands-on role for someone who has independently managed suspense, negotiated rebuttals, and understands how post-closing execution directly impacts cash flow, credibility, and risk.

This role operates post-close, with full authority once loans fund, and plays a critical role in protecting capital and scaling delivery operations.

Key Responsibilities

Delivery Ownership & Execution

  • Own end-to-end delivery of closed loans to investors and whole-loan purchasers, ensuring timely submission and purchase

  • Build and maintain investor-specific delivery checklists, eligibility gates, and suspense prevention controls

  • This role also owns the day-to-day execution and performance of offshore post-closing and delivery teams, ensuring work is completed accurately, on time, and in alignment with investor delivery standards.

  • Track and manage purchase timelines, days-to-cash, and aging inventory

Suspense, Rebuttals & Issue Resolution

  • Manage all investor suspense, rebuttals, and curative documentation through final purchase

  • Act as the primary escalation point for delivery disputes, exceptions, and delayed purchases

  • Partner with legal and compliance on complex delivery issues or investor challenges

Investor & Seller Communication

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for investor delivery and post-purchase review teams

  • Manage communications with correspondent sellers whose loans we purchase, including suspense requests, rebuttals, and resolution timelines

  • Ensure external communications are accurate, timely, and aligned with contractual and delivery requirements

Reporting, SLAs & Continuous Improvement

  • Own reporting on delivery performance, including first-pass purchase rates, suspense rates, rebuttal cycles, and cash timing

  • Set and enforce post-closing delivery SLAs, holding internal teams accountable

  • Perform root-cause analysis on delivery issues and drive process improvements to reduce repeat defects

Qualifications

  • 7+ years of post-closing and investor delivery experience, with flexibility for candidates who demonstrate deep, multi-investor ownership

  • Proven experience independently managing delivery, suspense, and rebuttals across multiple investors

  • Prior role as an escalation point for delayed purchases, delivery disputes, or investor exceptions

  • Experience designing, improving, or rebuilding post-closing and delivery workflows

  • Strong working knowledge of LOS platforms and investor delivery portals

  • Ability to track, analyze, and report on delivery performance metrics and cash timing

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with comfort engaging directly with investors and sellers

  • High attention to detail, strong judgment, and a bias toward ownership and accountability

What This Role Is Not

  • Not a checklist-only post-closing role

  • Not limited to document trailing or file indexing

  • Not a passive coordination position

  • This role owns outcomes: delivery quality, purchase timing, and issue resolution

Benefits

Ownership: Meaningful early-stage equity in Pylon
Healthcare: Top-tier medical, vision & dental with dependent support
401(k): Ability to save for your future
Flexible Time Off: Be on when you’re on and off when you’re off
Hardware Allowance: $2,000 to upgrade your workspace
Annual Off-sites: Fully paid team off-sites
At-cost Mortgages: Financing support for your next home

Join us in building America’s mortgage rails.

About The Role

We’re seeking an entrepreneurial Technical Oversight - Underwriting. This role involves both strategic oversight and hands-on management of third party fulfillment providers to ensure efficient, compliant loan origination while enhancing systems and workflows for high-quality, scalable operations.

You will be instrumental in shaping the future of our platform, developing underwriting workflows, standard operating procedures, and quality control measures. You will provide tactical guidance to engineering teams, emphasizing scalable human out of the loop solutions.

We are not a traditional mortgage lender. If you’re excited about building flexible automated systems with rigorous oversight that can scale, this role is for you.

About You

  • Possess expert-level knowledge of the entire mortgage lending process, detailed underwriting knowledge specific to loan requirements and comprehensive understanding of federal, state, and regulatory guidelines related to residential mortgage lending.

  • You are a visionary leader with a clear perspective on building scalable, modular origination infrastructure.

  • Comfortable operating in highly regulated industry whilst optimizing for performance. You build with a compliance first lens, respect regulations, continuously review, and update processes as needed.

  • Obsess over the customer and uphold the highest standard. You build for our customers and their borrowers, doing whatever it takes to make them successful on the platform.

  • Adhere to a scalable software first approach, operational workaround last. You surface issues, lead discussions around long-term solutions, document them, and manage temporary manual workarounds if needed.

  • Ability to oversee numerous 3rd party fulfillment partners, ensuring high quality, on-time originations. You build deep relationships and drive consistent results.

  • Have strong, principled opinions that you’re willing to defend. We have a culture of vigorous discussion and debate on decisions. We’ll push you to articulate your choices, and defend them where necessary.

  • Have great ideas, and lots of them. You should see opportunities all around you to make the product and team better. We’ll provide the environment to act on those ideas.

Key Responsibilities:

  • Develop and implement underwriting workflows, SOPs, SLAs, checklists, and QC measures to ensure high-quality and efficient loan underwriting.

  • Regularly access and enhance our Underwriting Systems to ensure smooth file flow, high quality, regulatory compliance and efficiency.

  • Oversee day-to-day operations with fulfillment partners, ensuring consistent loan delivery.

  • Define and monitor productivity standards and performance goals and ensure that they are met on a monthly, quarterly and annual basis.

  • Conducting 2nd level reviews, handling exceptions, and managing escalations to ensure quality control.

  • Act as a subject matter expert, aiding decision-making and driving product improvement.

  • Working closely with internal teams, partners, and engineering to drive product improvements and optimize the fulfillment infrastructure.

  • Provide technical and guideline training, recommend areas of improvement, and conduct ongoing training as needed.

  • Maintain a comprehensive understanding of mortgage origination and regulations to ensure compliance.

Requirements

  • 10+ years of experience in underwriting and managing underwriting teams across diverse loan types, including Conventional, Jumbo, NON-QM, GOVT across purchase and refinance.

  • Proven track record in developing underwriting workflows, SOPs, SLAs,and QC measures.

  • Proficiency in configuring Underwriting Systems for efficiency,quality and compliance.

  • Proven track record in managing and leading de-centralized underwriting teams.

  • Experience in the management of strategic 3rd party fulfillment partners.

  • Experience working on mortgage products within a fintech environment is strongly preferred.

Benefits

  • Ownership: Meaningful early-stage equity in Pylon.

  • Healthcare: Top-tier medical, vision & dental with support for dependents.

  • 401(k): Ability to save for your future.

  • Flexible Time Off: Be on when you’re on and off when you’re off.

  • Hardware Allowance: $2,000 to fix up your workspace.

  • Annual Off-sites: Fully paid for team off-sites in beautiful corners of the world.

  • At-cost Mortgages: We’ll help you finance your next home when you’re ready.

The Team

We're looking for Back End Engineers to join our API team. We treat our GraphQL API as a product — because it is one. Multiple customers build directly on top of it, and the quality of their experience is determined by how well we design, document, and maintain it.

Mortgage is a surprisingly rich domain to model. It's path-dependent: the choices you make early in a loan constrain what's possible later. It's nonlinear: different borrower situations branch into wildly different flows. Most APIs in this space paper over that complexity. We're building one that embraces it — encoding the real shape of mortgage into a surface that's impossible to misuse and delightful to build against.

Here Is What You'll Do

  • Define what a mortgage is in code. Seriously. You'll work on semantic models that don't just represent mortgages as they exist today — they expand what a mortgage can be. This is product design at the API layer.

  • Build toward an event-driven API. We're moving to a world where our API doesn't just respond to requests — it tells you what happened, why, and what you can do next. You'll help design and ship that future.

  • Make the complex feel simple. Our API should make the mortgage process impossible to get wrong. That means thoughtful abstractions, clear documentation, and an obsessive focus on developer experience.

  • Design for nonlinearity. Mortgage flows aren't linear wizards. Our future API encodes choice, branching, and path-dependence natively. You'll work on guided experiences that model real-world complexity without exposing it as chaos.

  • Treat this as a product surface. You'll think about breaking changes, versioning, onboarding, and the full lifecycle of an API that real companies depend on.

Join us in building America’s mortgage rails.

The role

Pylon has more demand than we can support. Our target customer is already watching. Thousands of originators in Facebook groups and online forums are talking about Pylon, curious about what we're building. We need someone who can build a movement and turn that curiosity into conviction.

Not through press releases or 12-week content calendars but through having a genuine point of view, knowing how platforms work at a mechanical level, and being willing to do things that feel a little insane.

This role is high-ownership and high-latitude. You'll have the budget to run real experiments, direct access to the founding team, and design resources to work with. You're also creative in your own right. The scope is intentionally broad and the best candidate will be excited by that.

What you'll own

Distribution

Build Pylon's audience from the ground up across X, LinkedIn, and wherever the conversation is actually happening. Own the channel strategy, grow the following, figure out what works and do more of it.

Content

Create content that earns attention: opinionated takes on the mortgage industry, showcasing our team and customers, original data and research, formats no one in this space has tried yet. You know the difference between a post that gets polite engagement and one that actually makes people think differently.

Founder presence

Work directly with our CEO to build his presence alongside your own. You'll help translate what Pylon knows about the mortgage industry into content that reaches customers, talent, and investors.

Experiments

Run growth experiments end-to-end: hypothesis, test, read the results, share what you learned. You'll have the budget and autonomy to test fast. Signal is more important than activity.

Community and earned media

Identify and activate the channels where our buyers actually are: communities, newsletters, podcasts, events. Build relationships with the writers, operators, and influencers who shape how people in mortgage and fintech think about infrastructure.

What we're looking for

  • You have taste. You know what great content looks like and why most of it misses.

  • You've grown something from zero (an account, a community, a product) and you know what actually made it work

  • You're fluent on social as a practitioner (not just a user). You understand how platforms distribute content and you engineer for it

  • You've grown a following from zero and can point to the specific moves that made it happen

  • You've actually built content systems using AI (vs used ChatGPT to write captions)

  • You can write arguments, narratives, and ideas that make people want to share them

  • You own the numbers: tracking what's working, why, and can report it back in a way that informs what comes next

  • You're comfortable being a face of the brand

What we're not looking for

  • Someone who needs approval to post

  • Someone who measures success by the size of a content calendar

  • Someone whose best case study is a rebrand

How to apply

Don't send a resume first. Send us something you made: a thread, a post, a campaign, a piece of content you're actually proud of. Tell us what you were trying to do and whether it worked. Tell us about a piece of content you didn't make but wish you had.

Many of us are former founders. We move quickly, challenge each other directly, and take full ownership of results. It’s hard work, but it will be worth it.

Join us in building America’s mortgage rails.

Why this role exists

We've outgrown an agency-and-contractor approach to hiring. It's expensive, it's fragmented, and it doesn't compound. We need someone to build Pylon's talent function as a real, owned, in-house engine: one that consistently lands exceptional engineers and operators, faster and cheaper than the market, and makes Pylon a place those people never want to leave.

You will be our first dedicated talent leader. You're not inheriting a machine; you're building one. If you do this well, you become one of the highest-leverage people in the company.

What you'll own

Build the in-house talent engine. Stand up sourcing, pipeline, and full-cycle recruiting as an internal capability. Wean us off contingent agencies and per-hire fees, build a sourcing motion that compounds, and hire/lead a small team (recruiters, sourcers, including offshore support) as volume demands.

Steward the culture. As we scale into our next phase of growth, you are a primary guardian of who we are: put customers first, think big, practice craftsmanship, deliver results. Protect the bar and the culture as the headcount grows.

Make engineering hiring the priority. Mortgages may be the hardest problem in tech: real money, real regulatory complexity, real stakes. Our engineers own entire systems, not tickets, and work across AI/ML and operations research. Your first mandate is landing more of them. Then scale the same rigor across GTM, operations, compliance, and G&A.

Own the full funnel and raise the bar. From first touch to signed offer: structured interviewing, calibrated scorecards, fast and decisive process, and a relentlessly high bar. Speed and craftsmanship are not in tension here; we expect both.

Build the employer brand and candidate experience. Make Pylon's story impossible to ignore to the people we want, and make every candidate interaction reflect "craftsmanship in everything," including the ones we don't hire. Own our careers' presence and how we show up in the market for talent.

Own onboarding, ramp, and retention. Hiring is half the job; keeping people is the other half. Standardize onboarding so new hires are productive on day one, and build the rituals, growth paths, and feedback loops that make great people stay and do their life's work here.

Run the systems and the numbers. ATS, hiring metrics, time-to-fill, pipeline health, headcount planning with leadership, comp and leveling frameworks, and the HR/onboarding ops stack (e.g. Rippling). Bring data, not vibes.

What we're looking for

  • You've built or substantially scaled an in-house talent function at a high-growth startup (ideally somewhere between seed and Series C), and you've done it for technical, hard-to-fill engineering roles in a competitive market.

  • You are high agency and a player-coach. You can personally source and close a brilliant, hard-to-get engineer and design the process that lets ten other people do it. You don't wait for a system to exist; you build it.

  • You think from first principles and you're contrarian-and-correct. You have strong opinions about hiring, you're right more than you're wrong, and you'll push back on leadership when you should.

  • You can sell a hard mission. You make ambitious people want to take a risk, and you tell Pylon's story in a way that resonates with the best.

  • You are data-driven about pipeline, conversion, comp, and headcount, comfortable owning the numbers in a board and investor context.

  • You care about culture and retention as much as req-filling. You measure success in great people who stay and do their best work, not just offers signed.

  • You thrive in-person, in ambiguity, at intensity. This is a hard, fast, high-stakes environment. You read "this will be hard" as a feature, not a warning.

Bonus:

  • Experience in fintech, infrastructure, or regulated industries.

  • A track record of cutting agency/contingent spend by building internal sourcing.

  • Experience standing up and managing offshore/distributed sourcing teams.

  • You've helped a company scale through a period of rapid growth and capital raises.

Your first 90 days (roughly)

  • 30 days: Learn the bar. Sit in on interviews, audit the current pipeline and spend, map open roles against our growth plan, and identify where we're losing candidates and money.

  • 45 days: Stand up the in-house sourcing motion, replace the most expensive contingent dependencies, ship a structured interview process and scorecards for engineering, and tighten onboarding.

  • 60 days: Have a measurable, compounding pipeline for engineering and key functions, a clear hiring plan and budget for the next phase of growth, and the first hires of your own team in motion.

What you get

  • Substantial ownership. Be a founder, not just an employee, with meaningful equity in Pylon.

  • Comprehensive health, dental, and vision for you and your dependents.

  • Access to Pylon's industry-leading home financing rates.

  • 401(k) and financial planning support.

  • The chance to build the team behind America's mortgage rails, and to make Pylon the place where the best people in the country want to do their life's work.

Compensation: competitive base + meaningful equity.

How we hire: our values

  • Put customers first. Hold yourself and others accountable to overdelivering for the people who depend on us. They're the reason we exist.

  • Think big. Default to first principles, question industry consensus, and refuse to be incremental. We're rebuilding a $13 trillion market.

  • Practice craftsmanship. Obsess over the details. Every pixel, every line of code, every candidate interaction matters.

  • Deliver results. Outcomes over optics. We measure ourselves by what we ship and move, not by activity.

If you're the kind of person who does their best work when the problem is hard and the stakes are real, this is your place. Join us.

Join us in building America’s mortgage rails.

Role Overview

Pylon is building software-driven mortgage processing. Rather than scaling a traditional processing department alongside loan volume, we are building a platform that automates routine diligence, document handling, workflow progression, and coordination.

As Head of Processing, you will bring deep mortgage-processing expertise into that system. You will own the operating model, exceptions, controls, and domain knowledge required to help Product and Engineering automate more of the work safely and accurately over time.

Responsibilities

  • Own processing domain expertise from submission through underwriting readiness.

  • Identify repetitive processing work that should be standardized, automated, or eliminated.

  • Translate processing workflows, edge cases, and expert judgment into product requirements and operating rules.

  • Build human-review queues, SLAs, escalation paths, and controls for unsupported or ambiguous cases.

  • Establish metrics for cycle time, manual touches, aging, exception rates, quality, and automated workflow coverage.

  • Partner closely with Account Management, Underwriting, Product, and Engineering.

  • Diagnose root causes behind aging, rework, bottlenecks, and automation failures.

  • Build training and operating systems for the human exception layer as volume grows.

Qualifications

  • Significant mortgage processing leadership experience at a scaled lender.

  • Strong preference for wholesale mortgage experience.

  • Experience operating at hundreds or thousands of loans per month.

  • Strong analytical and operational judgment.

  • Proven ability to improve throughput, quality, cycle time, or workflow design.

  • Comfortable making implicit operational knowledge explicit enough for technical teams to encode.

What success looks like

Pylon can materially increase monthly loan volume while the amount of routine human processing per loan declines. Human processors focus on the cases where judgment actually matters, and every recurring manual task becomes a candidate for product improvement.

The Role

This is not a seat in an established accounting department, it's a chance to build one. You'll be an early finance hire working directly with the CFO. Together we're designing an automation-first accounting function: an AI-native general ledger, warehouse funding optimization, and a modern loan origination system, integrated with our proprietary command center, under a controls framework built for SOC 1 Type II reporting and, ultimately, operate at a public-company 404(b) level of assurance.

You'll own day-to-day accounting operations end to end and then automate them. Every process you run is a process you'll help redesign for scale.

What You'll Own

  • Core operations — Full-cycle AP/AR, GL accrual accounting, and vendor mapping across the finance stack; own the monthly close calendar and drive it shorter every quarter.

  • Loan lifecycle — Loan-level accounting and diligence from lock to settlement — funding reconciliations, warehouse line activity, gain-on-sale, and investor settlement.

  • Controls — Execute and document internal controls designed for SOC 1 Type II reporting; partner with the CFO on IT audit design, evidence automation, and audit readiness.

  • Reporting — Build state-level and loan-level production metrics and ad hoc analyses in an AI-native reporting layer; deliver board- and lender-ready outputs.

  • Automation — Identify manual work and kill it — configure integrations, define system requirements, and test automation across the GL, LOS, warehouse funding, and command center systems.

  • Judgment — Make sound calls independently on classification, accrual, and process questions; escalate with a recommendation, not just a question.

Who You Are

  • 5–10 years of progressive experience with operational mortgage or structured credit depth — you've worked loan-level: a private credit fund managing non-QM pools, a whole-loan trading or aggregation shop, a mortgage originator's capital markets/accounting group, or similar.

  • Command of the FASB codification where it meets mortgages — ASC 310/320/860 (transfers and servicing), ASC 820/825 (fair value), derivatives and lock pipelines (ASC 815), CECL — and the judgment to shore up reporting where policy doesn't exist yet.

  • Big 4 foundation strong plus, not prerequisite; a top-university record and demonstrated rigor matter more than pedigree.

  • Proven operator at a high level — you've owned a close, an audit, or a system implementation, not just supported one.

  • Energized by AI-native tooling — you want to automate your own job's busywork, and you see an AI-first GL as an advantage, not a threat.

  • A builder's temperament: comfortable with ambiguity, willing to grind, and excited to learn from leadership with a proven track record.

Why This Role

  • Ground-floor build of a modern, automation-first finance function — the kind of experience that typically takes a decade to access.

  • Direct mentorship from a CFO with SEC/404(b)/Audit Committee experience and a CFO who has run finance at multiple lending platforms.

  • Clear growth path as Pylon scales: this role is designed to grow into broader leadership.

  • Remote-first flexibility with a high-ownership, high-trust culture.

What you’ll do

  • Embed with strategic customers, on site and remotely, to understand their teams, systems, and full mortgage workflow

  • Map how each customer works today, figure out where Pylon adds the most value, and put together a plan that gets them live quickly

  • Own each integration from scoping and solution design through data mapping, configuration, testing, and launch, working with their engineers and ours

About the role

Pricing is where mortgage deals are won or lost. A few basis points can decide whether a borrower gets the loan and whether our customers win the business. Our goal is the best pricing in the market, and we want to approach it with the rigor of a top hedge fund, using data, models, and a constant read on what the market is doing.

We’re hiring a Lead PM to own Capital Markets and Pricing. You’ll own how loans get priced, locked, and sold, from the rate a borrower sees to how the loan is executed in the secondary market. Because Pylon is vertically integrated, we can cut out a lot of the manual work and margin leakage that traditional lenders just accept, and pass those savings on to borrowers.

You’ll also build products that set us apart. That means finding gaps in the market, designing loan programs for borrowers others underserve, and launching them with our capital partners.

What you’ll do

  • Set the strategy for capital markets and pricing, and get product, engineering, and our capital markets team aligned on where we compete and how we win on price. You’ll also help grow the team

  • Own the roadmap for the pricing engine, product eligibility, rate locks, and secondary execution

  • Get us to the best pricing in the market by automating best execution across agency cash and MBS, aggregators, and whole loan buyers

  • Build pricing models and strategies with the rigor of a hedge fund, watching rate moves, spreads, investor appetite, and competitor pricing, and turning what you see into better prices

  • Write and ship code yourself, from pricing models and analysis to changes in the pricing engine

  • Design loan products competitors can’t easily copy, and work with investors and capital partners to bring them to market

  • Make pricing real-time and available through our API, so customers get every price, adjustment, and eligibility decision instantly, with a clear explanation behind each one

  • Cut cost and leakage across the loan lifecycle, including pull-through, lock extensions, fallout, pricing exceptions, and repurchase risk

  • Work with our capital markets team on hedging, pipeline risk, and warehouse capacity, and build tools that help them make faster, better calls

  • Build integrations with investors and counterparties for commitments, loan delivery, and loan sale

  • Make sure pricing is consistent, auditable, and compliant with fair lending and loan officer compensation rules, with clear governance over exceptions

  • Track what matters, like how our prices compare to the market, margin, win rate, and execution performance

  • Work with GTM and Account Management to support deals and make sure customers succeed

  • Use AI in your day-to-day work

About you

  • You have strong opinions and you’ll defend them. We argue about decisions a lot here, and we’ll ask you to explain your thinking and stand behind it. We also expect you to change your mind when someone shows you you’re wrong.

  • You’re ruthless about priorities. Every basis point comes with a tradeoff. You go after the biggest gains first, and you’re comfortable saying no to good ideas that come at the wrong time.

  • You’re comfortable in a heavily regulated market. Pricing has to be fair, consistent, and explainable, and compliance is non-negotiable for us. We work with regulators, we play by the rules, and we play to win.

  • You care a lot about our customers and their borrowers. Better pricing means real money saved for real families, and we’ll do whatever it takes to make our customers successful.

  • You’re obsessed with how the market moves. You follow rates, spreads, and investor behavior closely, you always want to know why things moved, and you’re always looking for ways to price better because of it.

  • You default to software over manual work. One of our guiding principles is that anything in the backend mortgage process done by a human is a bug, and capital markets still runs on a lot of spreadsheets, phone calls, and manual reconciliation. When we need a temporary workaround, you flag it, write it down, and push for the real fix.

  • You’re good with people. You’ll work with traders, investors, warehouse lenders, aggregators, and teams across Pylon, and you know how to build real relationships and get results through them.

  • You have a lot of ideas. You notice things that could be better about the product and the team, and we’ll give you room to act on them.

  • You’re willing to get into the weeds. You can pick up how mortgage capital markets work quickly, well enough to spot problems that veterans have stopped noticing.

Requirements

  • 4+ years in product management, or in a quantitative role like quant research, trading, or pricing at a hedge fund, bank, or trading firm

  • Very strong quantitative skills. You’ve built pricing or risk models, worked with real market data, and you’re fluent in SQL and Python

  • You’ve owned and scaled pricing, marketplace, payments, or other products where small changes in economics have a big impact

  • You write code and are comfortable committing to a production codebase, working alongside engineers on real-time pricing systems and integrations

  • You’ve built 0-1 products in a regulated industry

  • You’re hungry to learn mortgage capital markets from first principles until you’re fluent in pricing, secondary execution, and hedging

  • Nice to have: experience in mortgage capital markets, secondary marketing, pricing engines, or launching loan products

We don’t expect you to be a capital markets expert on day 1. We’ll bet on people who are hungry and learn fast. Over time, though, you’ll need to become one of the people the whole company trusts on pricing and execution.

Must live in or be willing to relocate to Palo Alto (CA) or New York City.

Mortgage is one of the most complicated products most people will ever use, and most mortgage software looks like it. You’ll change that. You’ll design and build the borrower application, borrower dashboards, loan officer tools, and the components customers embed in their own products. You’ll also build the design system that makes everything at Pylon feel fast, clear, and trustworthy.

What you’ll do

  • Design and build product experiences yourself, from early exploration to polished production interfaces, with no handoff in the middle

  • Own Pylon’s design system, including tokens, type, color, spacing, and a component library that makes it easy for any engineer to build something that looks great

  • Build components customers can theme and embed in their own products without losing quality, accessibility, or consistency

  • Take complicated workflows and dense mortgage data and make them easy to understand, using layout, hierarchy, interaction, and motion

  • Prototype in real code with real data, put it in front of borrowers, loan officers, and customers, and iterate quickly on what you learn

  • Get the details right, including states, edge cases, responsiveness, loading and empty states, keyboard interactions, and accessibility

  • Work closely with PMs and engineers, raise the design bar across the team, and help others improve their work through feedback and reusable patterns

  • Use AI and agentic coding tools throughout your process, from exploring ideas to shipping production interactions

About you

  • You have strong opinions and you’ll defend them, especially about craft. We argue about decisions a lot here, and we’ll ask you to explain your thinking and stand behind it. We also expect you to change your mind when someone shows you you’re wrong.

  • You’re ruthless about priorities. Every screen could be better. You focus on the details that matter most to users, and you’re comfortable saying no to good ideas that come at the wrong time.

  • You’re comfortable in a heavily regulated market. Disclosures, consent, and accessibility are part of the experience, and you design them to be clear instead of hiding them. We play by the rules, and we play to win.

  • You care a lot about borrowers, loan officers, and the lenders who serve them, and you hold a high bar for them. You notice the small things other people miss.

  • You default to software over manual work. One of our guiding principles is that anything in the backend mortgage process done by a human is a bug. Good design should take work off people’s plates whenever it can, and when an experience depends on a manual workaround, you call it out and push for the real fix.

  • You’re good with people. You’ll work with product, engineering, customers, and leadership, and you know how to build real relationships and get results through them.

  • You have a lot of ideas. You notice things that could be better about the product and the team, and we’ll give you room to act on them.

  • You’re willing to get into the weeds. You can learn mortgage quickly, to the point where you sound like you’ve been in the industry for 20 years.

This role isn’t for you if

  • You’d rather build other people’s designs than make design decisions yourself

  • You design in Figma and hand it off for someone else to build

  • You’re mostly interested in backend or infrastructure work

Requirements

  • 3+ years as a product designer who codes, a design engineer, or a frontend engineer who makes the design calls

  • A portfolio of live products or working prototypes with excellent visual and interaction work. This matters more to us than your title or years of experience

  • Great taste and strong fundamentals in typography, layout, hierarchy, color, interaction, and motion

  • Fluency in React, TypeScript, semantic HTML, and modern CSS, and the ability to ship production-quality frontend code

  • Experience building or leading a design system or component library, including tokens and theming

  • Comfort in Figma, mostly as a place to explore ideas

  • A strong grasp of accessibility and responsive design

  • Experience using AI and agentic coding tools in your design work

  • Nice to have: experience designing data-heavy or workflow-heavy products, especially in fintech, lending, or another regulated industry

We don’t expect you to be a mortgage expert on day 1. Over time, though, you’ll need to understand mortgage well enough to design for it with confidence.

Must live in or be willing to relocate to Palo Alto (CA) or New York City.

ABOUT THE ROLE

Agents are starting to do a lot of the work in mortgage, both at Pylon and at our customers. We’re hiring a Lead PM to own the Agent Platform, which is what every Pylon agent is built on and how outside agents work with Pylon.

The job has two halves. The first is internal. You’ll build the tools and infrastructure our engineers, operators, and business teams use to build, test, ship, and monitor agents, for everything from reading documents to underwriting to closing.

The second is external. Our customers are building their own agents, and you’ll make Pylon the easiest place for those agents to do real work. That means MCP servers, APIs designed with agents in mind, and the permissions and guardrails that keep it all safe.

What you decide here will shape how quickly we can automate the mortgage process, and how easily the rest of the industry can build on us.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Set the direction for agents across Pylon and get product, engineering, and operations aligned on where they’ll make the biggest difference

 - Own the roadmap for the platform’s core pieces, like tools, orchestration, context and memory, retrieval, evals, observability, and guardrails

 - Make it much faster for internal teams to go from an idea to an agent running in production, and give them shared patterns so nobody builds the same thing twice

 - Treat evals as a product of their own. Teams should have shared datasets, benchmarks, and regression checks, plus human review wherever a regulated decision needs it

 - Own how external agents work with Pylon, including MCP servers, APIs, scoped permissions, rate limits, and docs that both people and LLMs can follow

 - Make sure we can trace and explain every action an agent takes. We’d rather design for regulators from the start than bolt it on later

 - Make build or buy calls on models, vector databases, frameworks, and vendors, and keep an eye on cost, latency, and quality

 - Write and ship code yourself. You’ll commit to our codebase, build agents on the platform, and understand it the way its users do, which keeps the team close to what’s actually possible

 - Work with GTM and Account Management to help customers connect their agents to Pylon, support deals, and make sure customers succeed

 - Help hire and grow the team as the platform scales


ABOUT YOU

 - You have strong opinions and you’ll defend them. We argue about decisions a lot here, and we’ll ask you to explain your thinking and stand behind it. We also expect you to change your mind when someone shows you you’re wrong.

 - You’re ruthless about priorities. Our full stack approach means there’s always more to do than people to do it, so you keep the team on the highest-ROI work and you’re comfortable saying no to good ideas that come at the wrong time.

 - You’re comfortable in a heavily regulated market. Compliance is non-negotiable for us. We work with regulators to push the industry forward and get better outcomes for borrowers. We play by the rules, and we play to win.

 - You care a lot about our customers and their borrowers, and you hold a high bar for them. We’ll do whatever it takes to make them successful on Pylon.

 - You default to software over manual work. One of our guiding principles is that anything in the backend mortgage process done by a human is a bug. We can’t automate everything right away, so when we need a temporary workaround, you flag it, write it down, and push for the real fix.

 - You’re good with people. You’ll work with internal teams who want different things, engineers on the customer side, and a long list of model and tooling vendors, and you know how to build real relationships and get results through them.

 - You have a lot of ideas. You notice things that could be better about the product and the team, and we’ll give you room to act on them.

 - You’re willing to get into the weeds. You can learn mortgage well enough to sound like a 20-year veteran, and you keep up with AI research like someone who actually builds with it.


REQUIREMENTS

 - 4+ years as a product manager. An engineering background is a plus

 - You’ve owned and scaled a developer platform, infrastructure product, or API used by several teams or outside customers

 - You’ve shipped LLM-based agents or agent tooling to production and know your way around tool use, MCP, multi-agent orchestration, and structured outputs

 - You know evals well, including golden datasets, evals, LLM-as-judge, and regression testing, and you can connect model quality to business results

 - You understand retrieval, including RAG, embeddings, vector databases, chunking, hybrid search, and reranking

 - You understand the tradeoffs between prompt and context engineering, model choice, and fine-tuning, and how each one affects cost, latency, and accuracy

 - You’re familiar with tracing, guardrails, prompt injection, and protecting sensitive data like borrower PII

 - You write code and are comfortable committing to a production codebase, building prototypes, and going deep on architecture with engineers

 - You’ve built 0-1 enterprise software in a regulated industry

 - You can write SQL and define the metrics that show whether agents are working and whether teams are using the platform

 - Nice to have: mortgage or fintech infrastructure experience, or work on document understanding (OCR, extraction, classification)

We don’t expect you to be a mortgage expert on day 1. Over time, though, you’ll need to become one of the most trusted mortgage experts on the team to do this job well.

Must live in or be willing to relocate to Palo Alto (CA) or New York City.

Many of us are former founders. We move quickly, challenge each other directly, and take full ownership of results. It’s hard work, but it will be worth it.

Join us in building America’s mortgage rails.

About The Role

We’re seeking an entrepreneurial Mortgage Underwriter to join our Platform team. You’ll underwrite loans end to end and act as the expert human judgment behind our automated Decisioning engine, which ensures efficient, compliant loan origination.

You’ll work directly with customers on complex files and give hands-on feedback to our product and engineering teams. That feedback helps the platform handle more underwriting automatically over time.

We are not a traditional mortgage lender. If you’re excited about working with flexible automated systems with rigorous oversight that can scale, this role is for you.

About You

  • Possess expert-level knowledge of the entire mortgage lending process, detailed underwriting knowledge specific to loan requirements and comprehensive understanding of federal, state, and regulatory guidelines related to residential mortgage lending.

  • Comfortable operating in highly regulated industry whilst optimizing for performance. You build with a compliance first lens, respect regulations, continuously review, and update processes as needed.

  • Obsess over the customer and uphold the highest standard. You build for our customers and their borrowers, doing whatever it takes to make them successful on the platform.

  • Adhere to a scalable software first approach, operational workaround last. You surface issues, lead discussions around long-term solutions, document them, and manage temporary manual workarounds if needed.

  • Ability to oversee numerous 3rd party fulfillment partners, ensuring high quality, on-time originations. You build deep relationships and drive consistent results.

  • Have strong, principled opinions that you’re willing to defend. We have a culture of vigorous discussion and debate on decisions. We’ll push you to articulate your choices, and defend them where necessary.

  • Have great ideas, and lots of them. You should see opportunities all around you to make the product and team better. We’ll provide the environment to act on those ideas.

Key Responsibilities

  • Underwrite residential mortgage files across Conventional, Jumbo, Non-QM, and Government products, reviewing credit, income, assets, and collateral against guidelines.

  • Issue clear, accurate conditions and clear them promptly to reduce reconditioning and unnecessary submission turns.

  • Conduct 2nd level reviews, handle exceptions, and manage escalations to ensure quality control.

  • Regularly assess and enhance our Underwriting Systems to ensure smooth file flow, high quality, regulatory compliance and efficiency.

  • Act as a subject matter expert, aiding decision-making and driving product improvement.

  • Work closely with internal teams, partners, and engineering to drive product improvements and optimize the fulfillment infrastructure.

  • Maintain a comprehensive understanding of mortgage origination and regulations to ensure compliance.

Requirements

  • 3+ years of experience in underwriting across diverse loan types, including Conventional, Jumbo, Non-QM, and Government across purchase and refinance.

  • Experience working on mortgage products within a fintech environment is strongly preferred.
